changelog: Added three narrowly-scoped, low-risk positional rules to [When to Segment] that were shown safe by the critic's reference evidence: (1) segment right after a leading standalone discourse connective (그니까/그래서/근데/아니/그런데) when a full subject+predicate clause follows it, (2) explicitly extend the existing terminal-punctuation rule to embedded mid-sentence '?' followed by a summarizing clause, not just sentence-final '?', (3) segment immediately before an internal temporal connective (그러고 나서, 그 다음에) that introduces a second, distinct describable time span. These reposition/add boundaries without touching the -고 coordination wording, tag-question splitting, or filler-cluster splitting that were part of the previously rejected revision and likely caused its quality collapse.

Added a preliminary check to [Decision Procedure] step 1 requiring the three new [When to Segment] patterns (leading connective, embedded '?', internal temporal connective) to be tested explicitly before a long filler-laden sentence is left completely unsegmented, so latency is not left on the table on sentences with no other visible boundary — while leaving all existing rejection criteria (steps 2-7) unchanged.
